liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the Scarlet/Fire is worth hearing, and the recording is loud; a Star Trek rerun reminded them of it; Second set opens with Scarlet>Fire, after funky pre-Scarlet tuning that melts into a mellow vibe and stretches nicely into Fire [17][25]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): Dupree's>Smokestack>Deal in the first set is nice; the second Deal is a little sloppy but ends strongly [22]
- **Twilight Zone Theme** (1 other source): Twilight Zone Theme tuning occurs before Scarlet Begonias [6]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Samson sizzling, with long, great stretches before and after Drums [23]
- **She Belongs To Me** (1 review): Reviewer calls this their personal favorite version of She Belongs To Me [18]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin', Comes A Time and Around And Around all came before Drums; three encore songs followed Space [16]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): A real nice Comes A Time in the same set as She Belongs To Me [18]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 review): Reviewer considers this their favorite U.S. Blues ever [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-09-15.sbd.miller.34722.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 141 min; rated 3.22/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Distorted bass notes and static pops were repaired with Cool Edit Pro [1]
- **gd1985-09-15.177923.beyer.m88.terry.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 146 min [2]
- **gd85-09-15.aud.zelner.13600.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 136 min; rated 4.31/5 by 26 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording nice and good enough to convey the show [18]
- **gd1985-09-15.md421.coyotte.muletaper.88814.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 134 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [10]. Said about its sound: Deal cuts in but misses no music; From end of Big River through start of Smokestack, half the left channel intermittently drops out, slightly audible [10]
- **gd85-09-15.sbd.set2.walker.378.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 74 min; rated 4.31/5 by 13 [13]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording sounds good [22]

## Around the show

- Weather was blue sky and about 70 degrees with a slight breeze; the small venue resembled a high school football stadium ringed by trees [15]
- Security was nonexistent, and the band played the second set in shade, smiling, reluctant to leave the stage [15]
- Afternoon concert on a field at a small college, remembered as fun and full of surprises [16]
- The Twilight Zone tuning is notable because the band recorded the intro/outro music for the revived 1985-89 Twilight Zone TV series [20]
- Perfect weather, soft grass; first set started quiet, so the reviewer asked Healy at the soundboard to turn it up, and he did [23]
- Reviewer says this concluded a run of shows with a distinct atmosphere of sandy browns, dirty gold and dull Mars red [26]
- Reviewer, who attended, doubts Scarlet>Fire is the tour's best, since it faces stiff competition; U.S. Blues is too common to rank [21]
- Reviewer is surprised the show has few views compared with many weaker late-80s and early-90s shows [25]
- Scarlet/Fire here and at Red Rocks sound ancient to the reviewer; She Belongs To Me and Satisfaction are rarities [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-09-15.sbd.miller.34722.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [1]
- **gd1985-09-15.177923.beyer.m88.terry.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Terry; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Mark Terry's Master FOB Audience Cassettes; Beyer M88 mics > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell XLII-S90) [2]. Also: The Beyer M88 patches fill 0:07 in Deal and 0:22 in Comes A Time [2]
- **gd85-09-15.aud.zelner.13600.sbeok.shnf**: source: Unknown Mics (parabolic reflectors, 40 [8]
- **gd1985-09-15.md421.coyotte.muletaper.88814.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rick "Coyotte" Colyard; transferred by Muletaper; source: Sennheiser-MD421's>Sony D5>MAC [10]
- **gd85-09-15.sbd.set2.walker.378.sbeok.shnf**: source: reportedly SBD>CM>DAT>CDR [13]

claims.text: Weather was blue sky and about 70 degrees with a slight breeze; the small venue resembled a high school football stadium ringed by trees
Security was nonexistent, and the band played the second set in shade, smiling, reluctant to leave the stage
Truckin', Comes A Time and Around And Around all came before Drums; three encore songs followed Space
Afternoon concert on a field at a small college, remembered as fun and full of surprises
Reviewer says the Scarlet/Fire is worth hearing, and the recording is loud; a Star Trek rerun reminded them of it
Reviewer calls this their personal favorite version of She Belongs To Me
A real nice Comes A Time in the same set as She Belongs To Me
Reviewer finds the audience recording nice and good enough to convey the show
The Twilight Zone tuning is notable because the band recorded the intro/outro music for the revived 1985-89 Twilight Zone TV series
Reviewer considers this their favorite U.S. Blues ever
Reviewer, who attended, doubts Scarlet>Fire is the tour's best, since it faces stiff competition; U.S. Blues is too common to rank
Dupree's>Smokestack>Deal in the first set is nice; the second Deal is a little sloppy but ends strongly
Reviewer says the recording sounds good
Perfect weather, soft grass; first set started quiet, so the reviewer asked Healy at the soundboard to turn it up, and he did
Reviewer calls the Samson sizzling, with long, great stretches before and after Drums
Second set opens with Scarlet>Fire, after funky pre-Scarlet tuning that melts into a mellow vibe and stretches nicely into Fire
Reviewer is surprised the show has few views compared with many weaker late-80s and early-90s shows
Reviewer says this concluded a run of shows with a distinct atmosphere of sandy browns, dirty gold and dull Mars red
Scarlet/Fire here and at Red Rocks sound ancient to the reviewer; She Belongs To Me and Satisfaction are rarities
Soundboard from a PCM source via David Gans; patch source from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker
Distorted bass notes and static pops were repaired with Cool Edit Pro
Master cassette source from Mark Terry, transferred by Charlie Miller; Beyer M88 source from Charlie Connor supplies patches
The Beyer M88 patches fill 0:07 in Deal and 0:22 in Comes A Time
Twilight Zone Theme tuning occurs before Scarlet Begonias
Deal cuts in but misses no music
From end of Big River through start of Smokestack, half the left channel intermittently drops out, slightly audible
